drawings.description: figure : le treillis des drapeaux pour $n = 2$. En haut $D_{012}$ ; de lui descendent des flèches vers $D_{01}$, $D_{02}$, $D_{12}$, marquées « épi » ; de ceux-ci vers $D_0$, $D_1$, $D_2$, la flèche $D_{02} \to D_1$ barrée d'une croix, et « épi » sur plusieurs flèches
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. D012 on top, D01, D02, D12, then D0, D1, D2, with "épi" twice at the right. The three strokes from D012 have no visible arrowheads and are drawn as plain strokes; of the lower ones only D01 -> D1 carries a head. D02 -> D0 is one line drawn in two pieces (the upper piece forms a caret with the stroke from D02 towards D1), D12 -> D1, a short stroke from D12 towards D2. The only cross on the crop is a long stroke crossing a stroke that runs from below D12 down to the right, towards the foot of D2: it is not on the arrow D02 -> D1 where the transcription puts it; which arrow that crossed stroke is (perhaps D1 -> D2 or D12 -> D2) is a reading. Left out: a small struck mark between D0 and D1 and a small 4-like mark after D01, the line "D01 épi !!" above the lattice with its arrows and long underline (text of the page). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the crossed stroke under D12 lies on the line from D02 to D2 (it continues the right leg of the caret under D02, interrupted where the stroke D12 -> D1 passes), and D02 maps only to D0 and D2 in the lattice of flags, so the crossed arrow is D02 -> D2; the strokes are kept where they stand, and the transcription's « D02 -> D1 barrée » is to be corrected by the transcription skill. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan on a unit grid and measured (every stroke within 0.5 unit of its ink, every label centred on its letters); not compiled (no TeX in the session). No change needed: the seven nodes, the strokes between them with the one arrowhead, the crossed stroke and the two « épi » lie on the page where they are drawn. The small struck mark between D0 and D1 stays left out (struck text, not a figure); the line « D01 épi !! » above belongs to the text. Status set to ok.
drawings.disagreement: The cross of the transcription's « la flèche D02 -> D1 barrée d'une croix » stands on a stroke running from below D12 down towards D2, which is the arrow D02 -> D2 (D02 has no map to D1).

drawings.description: figure centrale : le même treillis dessiné plus grand, $D_{012}(F)$ en haut, $D_{02}(F)$, $D_{12}(F)$, puis $D_{01}$, $D_0$, $D_1$ et une case $\lbrace 1 \rbrace$ ; au-dessous une petite échelle encadrée « 2 3 4 5 ». À droite, un carré $D_{012} \to D_{12}$, $D_{02} \to D_2$, puis deux segments dessinés, l'un avec un point milieu, et « 23 ? »
drawings.kind: lattice of flags drawn larger; square; two segments
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. Left: D_I above; D012(F) on top, D02(F) and D12(F), then D01, D0, D1 and {1} (read with its braces, as the transcription has it); "épi" beside the arrow from D012(F) to D12(F). Strokes where they stand: a long stroke from D012(F) down to D01, a short one to D02(F), an arrow to D12(F) and a small point between them; under D02(F) two short strokes (no target); arrows from D12(F) down to D1 and to {1}, a third arrow into {1} from the left, a short arrow D01 -> D1, a stroke D01 -> D0 and a short stroke beside D0. The ladder "2 3 4 5" is marked by a heavy bar above 2, 3, 4 and a heavy bracket under 3, 4, 5 (not a closed box). The separating stroke, then at the right the square D012 -> D12, D012 - D02, D12 - D2, D02 -> D2, and the two segments with end ticks, the second with its point near the middle and its left half heavy; "2 3" and "?" under them. Still a reading: the targets of the short strokes under D02(F), which arrows carry heads (most strokes end without one). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the ladder « 2 3 4 5 » is not framed: a heavy bar stands above 2, 3, 4 (with a short drop at its right end) and a heavy bracket, with a short uptick at each end, under 3, 4, 5; there is no vertical stroke at the left, and the redraw is corrected to show this. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan on a unit grid and measured (every stroke within 0.5 unit of its ink; the ink left uncovered is the letters of the labels, which are typeset smaller than the hand, and the lines of text below the crop); not compiled (no TeX in the session). No change needed: the nodes, the strokes and arrows of the lattice, {1}, the bar and bracket of the ladder « 2 3 4 5 », the separating stroke, the square at the right and the two segments with their ticks and point lie on the page where they are drawn. Left out: a small mark like an « e » to the right of the arrows from D12(F), not in the transcription. Which of the short strokes under D02(F) are arrows remains a reading of the page, as said above. Status set to ok.

drawings.description: figure : un diagramme à deux étages. En haut $R_1'$, avec des flèches vers $F_0'$ et $F_1'$ ; de $F_0'$, $R_1'$, $F_1'$ descendent des flèches vers $R_1$, $F_0$, $F_1$, $F_2$ ; $R_1$ s'envoie sur $F_0$ et $F_1$. Le même diagramme est répété plus bas pour le cas 4), précédé de « $F_0$ »
drawings.notes: Upper diagram: R1' with arrows to F0' and F1'; from F0', R1', F1' strokes down to R1, F0, F1, F2; R1 -> F0, F1. Lower diagram, the same for case 4), with "4)" and "F0" above it; a small mark like "A" before F2 is left out. Short strokes without heads are drawn as on the page. The three small diagrams 1), 2), 3) at the top left of the sheet (3) heavily struck) are not part of this mark and are not drawn.

drawings.description: figure : un graphe, deux sommets cerclés reliés par une longue arête ; au premier pendent trois arêtes courtes ; le second, cerclé en bas, porte deux arêtes marquées d'un point milieu et une arête vers un troisième sommet cerclé, d'où partent trois arêtes formant un fuseau
drawings.kind: graph with ringed vertices and a spindle
drawings.notes: A ringed vertex with three short pendant edges, joined by a long arc to the right; a ringed vertex below carries two edges marked by a middle point and an edge (also with a middle point) to a vertex from which three edges form a spindle ending in a third ringed vertex at the top right. On the page the spindle starts from an unringed vertex and ends in the ringed one (the transcription puts the ring at the start).

drawings.description: au bas de la page, à gauche, sept petites figures sans lettres, exemples de 1-cartes : une boucle fermée sur un point ; un segment entre deux gros sommets ; un segment entre un gros sommet et un petit ; un « Y » dont deux bouts sont des sommets cerclés et le troisième un sommet plein ; un court segment isolé terminé par un point ; un disque dont le bord est une boucle issue d'un point, traversé par un arc issu du même point ; un sommet d'où partent quatre arêtes, deux épaisses entre lesquelles sont tracées des hachures.
drawings.kind: seven small figures: examples of 1-maps (loops, segments, a Y, a vertex with edges)
drawings.notes: As on the page, each figure through its own computed points: (1) a loop closed on a full point; (2) a segment between two heavy points, with a small tick at its middle; (3) a segment between a heavy point and a smaller one; (4) a Y: three arms from one centre, two ending in ringed points and the lower one in a full point; (5) a short isolated segment with a point at its upper end; (6) a full point with four strokes: an upper arc from the point to a tip at the top, an inner arc from just right of the point up to the same tip, and, from a small hook beside that tip, the outer loop round the right and the bottom back to the point and a second inner arc down to just right of the point (a disc bordered by a loop, cut by two inner arcs; the top is not closed, the tip and the hook stand 1.5 mm apart); (7) a full point with four edges: two heavy ones to the right, a longer thin one to the left ending in a small hook, a short thin one to the lower left, and six short hatching strokes between the two heavy edges. Left out: the formulas written under and beside them, which the transcription gives. The transcription's note says six figures and lists seven; it gives three edges to the last vertex where the page has four (the fourth is short and thin). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: figure 6 had one closed curve and one inner arc, the page has the four strokes above (the second inner arc was missing); figure 7 has six hatching strokes, not four; both corrected. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
drawings.disagreement: The note says « six petites figures » and lists seven; the last vertex has four edges on the page, not three.

drawings.description: en bas à droite, une figure : un arc qui monte puis file vers la droite jusqu'à une pointe, et sous lui quatre traits parallèles obliques ; sous les traits, les chiffres $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ ; plus bas $D_1$, $D_2$, et au-dessus de l'arc « — $D_3$ ».
drawings.kind: arc with four parallel strokes numbered 0 to 3
drawings.notes: As on the page: the arc rising from the lower left and running to a tip at the far right; five parallel oblique strokes under it, each starting near the left part of the arc: the upper four stop short of its upper part (the lower ones longer), the fifth, from the foot of the arc, runs up to the tip, closing the figure; the digits 0, 1, 2, 3 in a row under the upper strokes; D_1 and D_2 below them; « -- D_3 » above the arc. Left out: « 1, 1 + 1, 1 + 2 » with the vertical equality sign and the 2, at the right, and the formula below, which the transcription gives; the lattice arrows at the upper left of the crop (other drawings). The transcription's note speaks of an arrow towards D_3: the stroke before D_3 is a short dash. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw had four strokes, each 3 to 5 mm off its stroke on the page, and missed the long fifth one; the five strokes and the arc are now traced. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas à gauche, sous le petit diagramme : le dessin d'une boucle fermée sur un point.
drawings.notes: As on the page: a curve leaving a full point at the left and coming back towards it, drawn as he left it, with the small gap at the bottom (the stroke round the top and the right stops about 3.5 mm short of the stroke that leaves the point downwards). The long oblique strokes that strike the lower half of the page pass beside the loop and are not drawn; the loop itself is not struck. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw closed the loop; the gap is now drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à gauche de la fin de la démonstration, une petite figure sans lettres : un parallélogramme (un plan) traversé par un trait oblique qui le perce en un point marqué.
drawings.kind: parallelogram (a plane) pierced by a line at a marked point
drawings.notes: As on the page: the parallelogram in the four strokes he drew (the left side stops 6 mm short of the top side, and the right side stops 6 mm short of the bottom side, so two corners are open), the oblique line crossing it from above to below, and the heavy point on that line inside the parallelogram. No letters on the figure (the note of the transcription names the hyperplane H after the text). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw closed the parallelogram through four corners; the strokes are now drawn where they stand, open corners included. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, un petit carré dont les côtés portent $a$ (bas), $b$ (gauche), $c$ (haut), $d$ (droite), et au-dessous une lentille formée de deux arcs, « $a, c$ » au-dessus de l'arc supérieur, « $b, d$ » sous l'arc inférieur.
drawings.kind: square with named sides and a lens of two arcs (opposite sides identified)
drawings.notes: As on the page: the square between its four corners with the letters c (above), b (left), d (right), a (below) beside its sides; under it the lens, two separate arcs that nearly meet at the right and stand 3 mm apart at the left, with « a, c » above and « b, d » below. Agrees with the transcription's note. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw joined the two arcs at common end points; they are now drawn as they stand. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
